newsitem.title: CHINA: Mongolia copper smelter acid spill kills five.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia copper smelter acid spill kills five.

text.p: A spill of sulfuric acid from a Mongolian-U.S. joint venture copper smelter has killed five people, China's Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
The spill occurred last Wednesday at the Erdmin Copper Smelter in Orhon Province, a day before the $14 million joint venture came into production, Xinhua said, quoting local media reports.

The acid eventually spill spread up to 6 km (four miles) from the site, causing severe damage to the environment and to health, killing five people and prompting the local government to impose a state of emergency, Xinhua said.
The joint venture smelter is designed to produce about 3,000 tonnes of copper a year using locally available ore, it said.
The report gave no other details.
